docs.title: Cloud Bhutan eKYC
docs.text:
Enterprise-grade electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) verification platform built for Bhutan.

Cloud Bhutan eKYC provides a comprehensive suite of identity verification services including document OCR, face verification, liveness detection, fraud detection, AML screening, and more — all accessible through a simple REST API.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• :material-text-recognition: Document OCR

    Extract identity data from passports, CIDs, driving licences, and more with 80+ language support.

  • :material-face-recognition: Face Verification

    High-accuracy biometric face matching with 99.83% benchmark accuracy.

  • :material-shield-check: Liveness Detection

    6-layer passive liveness with ISO 30107 PAD conformance — anti-spoof, deepfake, depth, texture, and more.

  • :material-file-search: Fraud Detection

    Document tampering, photo substitution, copy/screen detection, and security feature validation.

  • :material-account-search: AML Screening

    PEP and sanctions screening against OpenSanctions with fuzzy name matching.

  • :material-nfc: NFC Chip Verification

    Read and validate e-Passport RFID/NFC chip data (DG1, DG2, SOD).

  • :material-video: Video KYC

    Recorded video verification with frame analysis, liveness, and face matching.

  • :material-workflow: Workflow Engine

    Configurable multi-step verification pipelines with branching logic.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Cloud-Bhutan/ekyc.git
cd ekyc

# Create virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Download ML models
python scripts/download_models.py

# Start the server
uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080

The API is now available at http://localhost:8080 with interactive docs at /docs.

docs.title: Verify Your First Identity
docs.text:
# 1. OCR a document
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ocr-document \
  -F "front_image=@passport.jpg"

# 2. Check liveness
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/liveness-check \
  -F "image=@selfie.jpg"

# 3. Match faces
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/verify-face \
  -F "passport_image=@passport.jpg" \
  -F "live_image=@selfie.jpg"

docs.title: eKYC API Reference
docs.text: Version: 1.0.0 · Last updated: March 2026 · Status: Proof of Concept

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The eKYC API provides a comprehensive suite of identity verification services including face verification, document OCR, liveness detection, fraud detection, AML screening, and more.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: http://localhost:8000/api/v1/

docs.title: API Versioning
docs.text:
Version Prefix Status v1 /api/v1/ Current, stable v2 /api/v2/ Identical to v1, ready for future divergence

You can also send an Accept-Version header (v1 or v2). All responses include an API-Version header. Deprecated endpoints return Deprecation: true, Sunset, and Link headers.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: POC Note: No authentication is required. A production deployment would require API keys, OAuth tokens, or mTLS.

docs.title: Content Types
docs.text: Scenario Content-Type Image uploads multipart/form-data JSON bodies application/json Mixed (image + form fields) multipart/form-data

docs.title: Supported Image Formats
docs.text: All image-accepting endpoints accept JPEG (image/jpeg) and PNG (image/png) only. Other formats return 400 Bad Request.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Tier Limit Applies To Standard 60 requests/minute per IP Most endpoints Heavy 10 requests/minute per IP Liveness, batch verify, face verify

Rate limit headers on every response:

Header Description X-RateLimit-Limit Requests allowed per window X-RateLimit-Remaining Requests remaining X-RateLimit-Reset Unix timestamp when the window resets

Exceeding the limit returns 429 with a Retry-After header.

docs.title: Response Envelope
docs.text:
Most endpoints return a flat JSON object. Errors follow this shape:

{
  "error": "Short error description",
  "detail": "Detailed explanation"
}

FastAPI validation errors (422):

{
  "detail": [
    {
      "loc": ["body", "field_name"],
      "msg": "field required",
      "type": "value_error.missing"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 1. Face Verification
docs.text: Endpoints for face comparison, detection, registration, 1:N search, duplicate detection, and age verification.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/verify-face
docs.text:
Compare a live photo against a passport/document photo.

Rate limit: Heavy (10/min)

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description passport_image file ✅ Passport or document photo (JPEG/PNG) live_image file ✅ Live selfie photo (JPEG/PNG)

Content-Type: multipart/form-data

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/verify-face \
  -F "passport_image=@passport.jpg" \
  -F "live_image=@selfie.jpg"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "match": true,
  "confidence": 0.9234,
  "distance": 0.3812,
  "threshold": 0.4,
  "face1_detected": true,
  "face2_detected": true
}

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text: Status Condition 400 Unsupported file type 422 Missing required file 429 Rate limit exceeded

docs.title: POST /api/v1/detect-faces
docs.text:
Detect all faces in an image with bounding boxes and confidence scores.

Rate limit: Standard (60/min)

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description image file ✅ Image to analyze (JPEG/PNG)

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/detect-faces \
  -F "image=@photo.jpg"

docs.title: POST /api/v1/register-face
docs.text:
Register a face embedding in the database for 1:N matching.

Rate limit: Standard (60/min)

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description image file ✅ Face image (JPEG/PNG) identity_id string ❌ Unique identifier for this person. Auto-generated if omitted

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/register-face \
  -F "image=@face.jpg" \
  -F "identity_id=USER-001"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "identity_id": "USER-001",
  "registered": true,
  "face_detected": true,
  "embedding_stored": true
}

docs.title: POST /api/v1/search-face
docs.text:
Search the face database for matches (1:N comparison).

Rate limit: Standard (60/min)

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description image file ✅ — Face image to search (JPEG/PNG) threshold float ❌ 0.4 Similarity threshold (lower = stricter) top_k int ❌ 5 Maximum number of results

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/search-face \
  -F "image=@probe.jpg" \
  -F "threshold=0.35" \
  -F "top_k=3"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "query_face_detected": true,
  "matches": [
    {
      "identity_id": "USER-001",
      "distance": 0.2815,
      "confidence": 0.9543
    }
  ],
  "total_matches": 1
}

docs.text:
Check if a face already exists in the database.

Rate limit: Standard (60/min)

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description image file ✅ — Face image (JPEG/PNG) threshold float ❌ 0.4 Distance threshold for duplicate match

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:

  -F "image=@face.jpg" \
  -F "threshold=0.35"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "is_duplicate": true,
  "matched_identity": "USER-001",
  "distance": 0.2103,
  "confidence": 0.9712
}

docs.title: POST /api/v1/verify-age
docs.text:
Estimate age from a face image and compare against a date of birth.

Rate limit: Standard (60/min)

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description image file ✅ Face image (JPEG/PNG) date_of_birth string ✅ Date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:

  -F "image=@face.jpg" \
  -F "date_of_birth=1990-05-15"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "estimated_age": 33,
  "document_age": 35,
  "age_difference": 2,
  "match": true,
  "confidence": 0.82,
  "tolerance_years": 5,
  "detection_score": 0.9945,
  "error": null
}
Field Type Description estimated_age int \| null ML-estimated age from face document_age int \| null Calculated age from DOB age_difference int \| null Absolute difference match bool Whether difference ≤ tolerance_years confidence float Age estimation confidence tolerance_years int Allowed deviation (default 5)

docs.title: 3. Liveness Detection
docs.text: Detect presentation attacks (printed photos, screens, masks) and deepfakes.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/liveness-check
docs.text:
Check if a face image is from a live person or a spoof attempt. Includes ISO 30107-3 PAD (Presentation Attack Detection) conformance data.

Rate limit: Heavy (10/min)

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description image file ✅ Face image (JPEG/PNG)

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/liveness-check \
  -F "image=@selfie.jpg"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "is_live": true,
  "liveness_score": 0.9421,
  "checks": {
    "texture": { "score": 0.95, "passed": true },
    "frequency": { "score": 0.91, "passed": true },
    "color": { "score": 0.97, "passed": true },
    "edge": { "score": 0.93, "passed": true }
  },
  "iso_30107": {
    "pad_level": "Level_2",
    "apcer": 0.032,
    "bpcer": 0.015,
    "acer": 0.0235,
    "attack_types_detected": [],
    "conformance_passed": true,
    "threshold_used": 0.5
  }
}
Field Description is_live Whether the image passes liveness liveness_score Overall liveness confidence (0–1) checks Per-layer analysis (texture, frequency, color, edge) iso_30107.pad_level PAD conformance level iso_30107.apcer Attack Presentation Classification Error Rate iso_30107.bpcer Bona Fide Presentation Classification Error Rate

docs.title: POST /api/v1/check-deepfake
docs.text:

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description image file ✅ Face image (JPEG/PNG)

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:

  -F "image=@suspicious.jpg"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{

  "confidence": 0.9712,
  "face_detected": true,
  "face_bbox": [102, 65, 310, 340],
  "ml_detection": {
    "is_deepfake": false,
    "confidence": 0.9712,
    "face_detected": true,
    "model": "vit_deepfake_detector"
  },
  "heuristic_detection": {
    "is_deepfake": false,
    "confidence": 0.8530,
    "face_detected": true,

docs.title: 5. Batch Processing
docs.text: Submit multiple documents for asynchronous batch verification with job tracking.

docs.text:

docs.title: Request
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description images file[] ✅ Document images, 1–20 files (JPEG/PNG)

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/batch/verify \
  -F "images=@doc1.jpg" \
  -F "images=@doc2.jpg" \
  -F "images=@doc3.jpg"

{

docs.title: Key Design Patterns
docs.text:
• FastAPI + Service Layer — Routers handle HTTP concerns (validation, file uploads, response formatting). Services contain all business logic and ML inference. Routers access services via request.app.state.<service>.
  • Lifespan Startup — All ML models are loaded once during application startup using FastAPI's lifespan context manager. This avoids cold-start delays on individual requests.
  • In-Memory Stores (POC) — Face database, webhook registry, consent records, analytics events, batch jobs, and workflow definitions all live in Python dictionaries/deques. In production, replace with Redis, PostgreSQL, or equivalent persistent stores.
  • Singleton Services — AMLScreeningService and AnalyticsService use the singleton pattern (__new__) to share state across the application.

docs.title: Router → Service Pattern
docs.text:
Every router follows the same pattern:

# In router (e.g., app/routers/verification.py)
@router.post("/verify-face")
async def verify_face(request: Request, ...):
    service = request.app.state.face_service  # Access service from app state
    result = service.compare_faces(image1, image2)  # Delegate to service
    return result  # Return as JSON

Services are instantiated once in main.py's lifespan() and stored on app.state.

docs.title: 4.1 Face Verification (face_verification.py)
docs.text:
What it does: 1:1 face comparison, multi-face detection, and 1:N face search against an in-memory database.

Key algorithms: - InsightFace buffalo_l — ArcFace-based face recognition model providing 512-dimensional embeddings - Cosine similarity for face matching (threshold: 0.4) - Largest-face selection when multiple faces are present

Capabilities: - compare_faces() — 1:1 match between two images - detect_faces() — Detect all faces with age, gender, bounding box - register_face() / search_face() — In-memory face database for 1:N search - detect_duplicate() — Check if a face already exists in the database

Dependencies: insightface, onnxruntime, numpy, opencv-python-headless

docs.title: 4.2 Liveness Detection (liveness.py)
docs.text:
What it does: 6-layer presentation attack detection combining ML models and signal analysis.

Layers and weights:

Layer Weight Method ML Anti-Spoof 0.35 anti-spoof-mn3 (MobileNetV3, ONNX) — trained on CelebA-Spoof Deepfake 0.20 Deep-Fake-Detector-v2 (ViT-B16, ONNX) Context 0.20 Scene analysis — background consistency, lighting Depth 0.10 MediaPipe Face Landmarker — 478 landmarks with z-depth Texture 0.08 Pixel-level texture analysis (LBP, noise patterns) Color/Frequency 0.07 Moiré detection, color banding, FFT analysis

Threshold: Combined score ≥ 0.45 = live

Model auto-download: The anti-spoof model is downloaded from OpenVINO Model Zoo on first use. MediaPipe's Face Landmarker task file is also auto-downloaded.

Dependencies: onnxruntime, mediapipe, opencv-python-headless, numpy

docs.title: 4.3 Deepfake Detection (deepfake_detection.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Classifies face images as real or deepfake using a Vision Transformer.

Model: Deep-Fake-Detector-v2 (ViT-base-patch16-224), ONNX format (~343 MB) - Source: HuggingFace onnx-community/Deep-Fake-Detector-v2-Model-ONNX - Labels: {0: "Realism", 1: "Deepfake"} - Preprocessing: resize to 224×224, rescale to [0,1], normalize (mean=0.5, std=0.5)

Face extraction: Uses Haar Cascade (haarcascade_frontalface_default.xml) for lightweight face cropping before classification.

docs.title: 4.4 Document OCR (document_ocr.py + passport_ocr.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Auto-detects document type (passport, ID card, driving license) and extracts structured fields.

Processing pipeline: 1. Document type detection — Analyzes aspect ratio, MRZ presence, and text patterns 2. MRZ extraction (passports) — Multi-strategy via mrz_detector.py: - PassportEye direct detection - PaddleOCR text → MRZ reconstruction - Geometric crop + re-read 3. VIZ extraction — Regex-based field extraction from OCR text (names, dates, document numbers, CID for Bhutanese documents) 4. PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5 — Text extraction engine for non-MRZ regions

Supported documents: - Passports (MRZ TD3 format) - National ID cards (including Bhutanese CID) - Driving licenses - Front + optional back page

Dependencies: paddleocr, paddlepaddle, passporteye, opencv-python-headless

docs.title: 4.5 Fraud Detection (fraud_detection.py)
docs.text:
What it does: 4-check forensic analysis of document images.

Check Weight Technique Fake Document 0.30 ELA (Error Level Analysis), EXIF validation, edge artifacts, colour consistency Photo Substitution 0.25 Compression analysis, lighting consistency, boundary artifacts Tampering 0.25 Font consistency, spacing analysis, field-level forensics Copy/Screen 0.20 Moiré pattern detection, colour distribution, DPI analysis

Thresholds: Each check has an individual threshold (0.50–0.55). The overall fraud score is a weighted average; ≥ 0.55 = flagged as fraudulent.

No ML models — Pure computer vision and statistical analysis.

docs.title: 4.6 Security Features (security_features.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Validates physical document security features.

  • Watermarks — FFT-based frequency analysis for subtle patterns
  • Hologram regions — HSV saturation analysis for iridescent regions
  • Microprint — Edge density analysis in expected microprint zones
  • Document structure — Layout conformity validation

A document is considered to have security features if ≥ 2 of 4 checks pass.

docs.title: 4.7 AML Screening (aml_screening.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Fuzzy name matching against the OpenSanctions consolidated dataset.

Data source: https://data.opensanctions.org/datasets/latest/default/entities.ftm.json - Downloaded to data/sanctions/entities.ftm.json - Parsed into in-memory entity index (singleton pattern)

Matching algorithm: - Unicode normalization (NFKD, strip diacritics) - Token-set overlap scoring - Levenshtein distance (pure Python implementation, no external deps) - Configurable match threshold

Entity types screened: Persons, organizations — covers sanctions, PEPs, and crime watchlists.

docs.title: 4.8 NFC Verification (nfc_verification.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Parses ICAO 9303 e-Passport NFC chip data.

Supported Data Groups: - DG1 — MRZ data (TLV parsing → tag 0x5F1F, then MRZ validation with check digits) - DG2 — Face biometric (CBEFF container → JPEG/JP2 extraction) - SOD — Security Object Document (ASN.1 structure validation via asn1crypto)

Cross-verification: Can compare DG2 face against a selfie using the FaceVerificationService.

Dependencies: asn1crypto

docs.title: 4.9 Video KYC (video_kyc.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Processes uploaded video for identity verification.

Pipeline: 1. Create a session → receive session_id 2. Upload video (MP4/WebM/QuickTime, max 50 MB, max 30 seconds) 3. Frame extraction via OpenCV 4. Per-frame analysis: liveness check, face consistency, scene change detection 5. Optional face matching against a reference image

In-memory sessions with automatic state tracking (created → processing → completed/failed).

docs.title: 4.10 Workflow Engine (workflow_engine.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Orchestrates ordered sequences of verification steps.

Step types: ocr, liveness, face_match, fraud_check, age_verify

Workflow definition: 

{
  "name": "Standard KYC",
  "steps": [
    {"name": "Extract Document", "type": "ocr", "on_fail": "stop"},
    {"name": "Check Liveness", "type": "liveness", "on_fail": "stop"},
    {"name": "Match Face", "type": "face_match", "on_fail": "stop"},
    {"name": "Fraud Analysis", "type": "fraud_check", "on_fail": "continue"}
  ]
}

Failure handling: Each step can be configured with on_fail: stop (abort workflow), skip (proceed to next), or continue (proceed but flag).

Execution tracking: Each execution gets a unique ID with per-step status, duration, and results.

docs.title: 4.11 Analytics (analytics_service.py)
docs.text:
What it does: In-memory event tracking with a 10,000-event ring buffer.

Time windows: 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d

Tracked metrics: - Event counts by type - Verification pass/fail rates - Fraud detection counts - Latency percentiles (when duration_ms is provided)

docs.title: 4.12 Webhooks (webhook_service.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Registers callback URLs and delivers event payloads with HMAC-SHA256 signatures.

  • Register webhooks for specific event types
  • Automatic retry (3 attempts with exponential backoff)
  • Payload signing: HMAC-SHA256(payload, secret) in the X-Webhook-Signature header
  • In-memory registry (POC — not persistent)

docs.title: 4.13 Device Fingerprint (device_fingerprint.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Extracts risk signals from HTTP request headers.

Signals detected: - Emulator (BlueStacks, Nox, Genymotion, etc.) - Bot/automation (Selenium, Puppeteer, Playwright, curl) - Headless browser markers - Datacenter IP ranges (AWS, GCP, Azure CIDRs) - User-Agent anomalies

Output: Risk score (0–100) with flags and recommendation (allow, challenge, deny).

docs.title: 4.14 Geo Risk (geo_risk.py)
docs.text:
What it does: IP geolocation risk assessment using ip-api.com (free tier, 45 req/min).

Signals: - Proxy/VPN detection (weight: 30) - Hosting/datacenter IP (weight: 25) - Country mismatch against expected nationality (weight: 35) - High-risk country list (configurable, weight: 10)

Caching: In-memory, 1-hour TTL per IP.

docs.title: 4.15 Consent Management (consent_service.py)
docs.text:
What it does: TTL-based consent records with revocation support.

Consent purposes: identity_verification, biometric_processing, data_storage

Lifecycle: Grant → validate → revoke. Records expire automatically based on duration_hours. Revocation triggers registered purge callbacks.

docs.title: 4.16 Batch Processing (batch_service.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Async job queue for processing up to 20 documents concurrently.

  • ThreadPoolExecutor with 4 workers
  • Job TTL: 1 hour (auto-cleanup)
  • Poll-based status tracking: pending → processing → completed/failed
  • Each document runs OCR + fraud detection independently

docs.title: 4.17 Age Estimation (age_estimation.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Estimates age from face images using InsightFace's built-in age attribute.

  • Reuses the same buffalo_l model instance as FaceVerificationService (no duplicate loading)
  • verify_age() — Compares estimated age against a provided date of birth (±5 year tolerance)

docs.title: 4.18 PAD Conformance (pad_conformance.py)
docs.text:
What it does: Maps liveness scores to ISO 30107-3 PAD levels.

Liveness Score PAD Level APCER Estimate BPCER Estimate ≥ 0.85 Level 3 1% 15% ≥ 0.60 Level 2 5% 10% ≥ 0.30 Level 1 20% 5% < 0.30 None 100% 0%

Attack classification: Print, replay (screen), mask, deepfake — based on per-layer score decomposition.

docs.title: GPU vs CPU Execution
docs.text:
By default, all ONNX models use CPUExecutionProvider. To enable GPU:

  1. Install CUDA-compatible ONNX Runtime: 

    pip install onnxruntime-gpu

  2. The services will automatically use CUDAExecutionProvider if available. To verify: 

    curl http://localhost:8080/debug/gpu

The /debug/gpu endpoint reports: - PyTorch CUDA availability - ONNX Runtime available providers - PaddlePaddle GPU status - InsightFace active providers

docs.title: API Versioning
docs.text:
Strategy: Both v1 and v2 are mounted from the same routers, allowing future divergence.

/api/v1/*  ← Current stable API
/api/v2/*  ← Future version (currently identical to v1)

Accept-Version Header: - Clients can send Accept-Version: v1 or Accept-Version: v2 - Default: v1 - Invalid values fall back to v1

Response Headers: | Header | Description | |---|---| | API-Version | The version that handled the request | | Deprecation | true if the endpoint is deprecated | | Sunset | Date when a deprecated endpoint will be removed | | Link | Successor endpoint URL (for deprecated endpoints) |

Configuring Deprecations:

In app/middleware/versioning.py, add entries to DEPRECATED_ENDPOINTS:

DEPRECATED_ENDPOINTS = {
    "/api/v1/old-endpoint": {
        "date": "2026-06-01",
        "successor": "/api/v2/new-endpoint"
    },
}

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Powered by SlowAPI (built on limits library).

Tier Limit Applies To Default 60 requests/minute All endpoints Heavy 10 requests/minute Liveness, batch, face verification

Rate limit headers (on every response): - X-RateLimit-Limit - X-RateLimit-Remaining - X-RateLimit-Reset

429 Response: 

{
  "error": "Rate limit exceeded",
  "detail": "10 per 1 minute",
  "retry_after": 60
}

Rate limits are keyed by client IP (get_remote_address).

docs.title: Stateless Processing
docs.text: This POC processes images in-memory and returns results immediately. No images or biometric data are written to disk during normal operation (except temporary files for video processing, which are deleted after use).

docs.title: In-Memory Only (POC Limitation)
docs.text:
All state (face database, webhooks, consent records, analytics, batch jobs, workflow definitions) is stored in Python data structures and lost on restart. For production:

Component Production Alternative Face database PostgreSQL + pgvector, or Milvus/Pinecone Webhooks PostgreSQL + message queue (RabbitMQ, SQS) Consent records PostgreSQL with audit logging Analytics ClickHouse, TimescaleDB, or cloud analytics Batch jobs Celery + Redis, or cloud job queues AML data Dedicated compliance platform

docs.title: TLS
docs.text: The application serves HTTP. Always deploy behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, cloud load balancer) in production.

docs.title: Consent Management
docs.text: The consent service provides a framework for recording user consent before biometric processing. In production, integrate with your legal/compliance infrastructure and ensure GDPR/data protection compliance.

docs.title: PII Handling
docs.text:
• OCR results contain PII (names, dates, document numbers)
  • Face embeddings are biometric data
  • Ensure proper data handling policies in production
  • Consider encryption at rest and in transit

docs.title: Scaling Considerations

• Single worker is recommended due to in-memory state. Multiple workers would have separate state.
  • For horizontal scaling, externalize state to Redis/PostgreSQL first.
  • Memory: Expect 2–4 GB RAM per instance with all models loaded.
  • CPU: ML inference is CPU-bound; 2+ vCPUs recommended.

  | jq '{is_live: .is_live, score: .overall_score}'

# Step 3: Match document photo against selfie
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/verify-face \
  -F "passport_image=@id_card.jpg" \
  -F "live_image=@selfie.jpg" \
  | jq '{match: .match, score: .score}'

docs.title: Full Workflow: OCR → Liveness → Face Match → Fraud Check
docs.text:
import requests

BASE = "http://localhost:8080/api/v1"

# 1. OCR
with open("passport.jpg", "rb") as f:
    ocr = requests.post(f"{BASE}/ocr-document", files={"front_image": f}).json()
print(f"Name: {ocr.get('extracted_data', {}).get('full_name')}")

# 2. Liveness
with open("selfie.jpg", "rb") as f:
    live = requests.post(f"{BASE}/liveness-check", files={"image": f}).json()
print(f"Live: {live['is_live']} (score: {live['overall_score']})")

# 3. Face match
with open("passport.jpg", "rb") as doc, open("selfie.jpg", "rb") as selfie:
    match = requests.post(f"{BASE}/verify-face",
        files={"passport_image": doc, "live_image": selfie}).json()
print(f"Match: {match['match']} (score: {match['score']})")

# 4. Fraud check
with open("passport.jpg", "rb") as f:
    fraud = requests.post(f"{BASE}/detect-fraud", files={"image": f}).json()
print(f"Fraudulent: {fraud['is_fraudulent']} (score: {fraud['overall_score']})")

        files={"document_image": doc, "selfie_image": selfie}).json()

docs.title: Model Download Issues
docs.text:
• Slow downloads: Models are large (343 MB for deepfake). First startup may take several minutes.
  • Network errors: If download fails mid-way, delete the partial file from models/ and restart.
  • Proxy/firewall: Ensure access to:
  • https://storage.openvinotoolkit.org (anti-spoof model)
  • https://huggingface.co (deepfake model)
  • https://github.com/deepinsight/insightface (InsightFace models)

docs.title: Memory Requirements
docs.text: Configuration RAM Minimum (all models loaded) ~2 GB Recommended 4 GB With large AML dataset loaded 4–6 GB Batch processing (20 docs) 4–8 GB

docs.title: numpy / OpenCV Version Conflicts
docs.text:
The project pins numpy>=1.24.0,<2.0.0 to avoid breaking changes in numpy 2.x. If you see:

AttributeError: module 'numpy' has no attribute 'float'

Ensure numpy < 2.0: 

pip install "numpy>=1.24.0,<2.0.0"

docs.title: skimage.transform.rescale multichannel Error
docs.text: PassportEye uses a deprecated multichannel parameter. The app monkey-patches this in passport_ocr.py. If you still see errors, ensure scikit-image<0.21.0.

docs.title: HEIC Image Support
docs.text:
HEIC/HEIF images are supported if pillow-heif is installed. The app registers the HEIF opener at startup. Without it, HEIC uploads will fail.
